title: Objectify, Don't Delete: Complaint-Derived Evaluation of Ambient Clinical Notes
abstract: arXiv:2611.19525v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evaluating the quality of AI-generated clinical notes is hard: standard metrics like ROUGE measure lexical similarity to reference notes, while expert checklists encode what committees believe matters. Neither captures what clinicians actually complain about. Recent work has shown that evaluation criteria can be mined from user feedback and filtered to criteria that LLM judges can reliably enforce. We argue that this is where much of the value is lost. The criteria that fail enforceability are disproportionately the ones clinicians raise most often, because high-frequency complaints are stated as several questions glued together. No yes/no judgment can grade such composites as posed. We introduce an objectification step that rewrites such criteria into sets of scoped, determinate decisions. We demonstrate the approach through an evaluation pipeline that mines criteria from complaints, objectifies them, and deploys LLM judges against both

translated_title: 对象化而非删除：基于临床医生投诉的AI环境式临床记录评估
translated_abstract: 评估AI生成的临床记录的质量是困难的：像ROUGE这样的标准指标衡量的是与参考记录之间的词汇相似度，而专家清单则编码了委员会认为重要的内容。这两者都无法捕捉临床医生真正抱怨的问题。近期的研究表明，评估标准可以从用户反馈中挖掘出来，并过滤至LLM评判者能够可靠执行的标准。我们认为，这正是大量价值流失的地方。那些未能通过可执行性检验的标准，恰恰是临床医生最常提出的标准，因为高频抱怨往往以多个问题捆绑在一起的形式陈述。任何是非判断都无法对这样的复合问题进行评分。我们引入了一个“对象化”步骤，将此类标准改写为一组范围明确、界限清晰的具体决策。我们通过一个评估流程展示了这一方法：该流程从投诉中挖掘标准、对其进行对象化，并部署LLM评判者对两者进行评估。
tldr: 该论文提出一个“对象化”步骤，将临床医生高频抱怨中捆绑的复合问题改写为一组范围明确、可判定的是非决策，从而保留那些原本会被可执行性过滤环节丢弃的投诉标准，并将其用于LLM评判的AI临床记录质量评估。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an "objectification" step that rewrites clinicians' high-frequency complaints—posed as composite questions glued together—into sets of scoped, determinate yes/no decisions, preserving criteria that would otherwise be discarded by enforceability filtering for LLM-judge evaluation of ambient clinical notes.
